summary: Iteration 2 re-test of Træningsmester landing page focused on the 5 user-flagged items (brand colors, pillars scroll-scrub + pinning, footer wordmark, mobile friendliness, count-up stats, custom cursor) plus regression on waitlist validation + 1 live Supabase happy-path. 4 of the 5 user complaints are NOW CORRECT. The pillars 'Tre faser' SCRUB LOGIC works (active class & rail width progress 0→1→2 with crossfading phone opacities) but the SECTION DOES NOT VISUALLY PIN on desktop — position:sticky is being defeated by 'html{overflow-x:hidden}' at /app/src/styles.css line 57, so the phone scrolls away with the page instead of staying centered. This is the user's #1 complaint and is still functionally broken visually.

ui_bugs.issue: position:sticky;top:0 is NOT pinning the phone in viewport on desktop (1440x900). Measured pin.getBoundingClientRect().top tracks wrap.top (e.g. -1153px when wrap is at -1153px) instead of staying at 0 inside the sticky range. Root cause: ancestor 'html { overflow-x:hidden }' at /app/src/styles.css line 57 (and likely body line 63) makes <html> the scroll container, which is a well-known killer of position:sticky on descendants. The scrub LOGIC works (activeNav 0→1→2, rail width 0→637.5/637.5px, phone shot opacities crossfade in sync) — only the visual pinning fails, so users see the whole pillar block scroll past normally instead of the phone staying centered.

action_items: HIGH: Fix position:sticky on .pillars-pin. The pin scrolls with the page on desktop. Root cause is 'overflow-x:hidden' on <html> at /app/src/styles.css:57 (and the same rule on <body> at line 63). Recommended fix: remove overflow-x:hidden from <html> (keep it only on <body> if needed) AND find the actual element that is leaking horizontally (most likely .hero-canvas, .trust marquee, or the footer wordmark itself) and constrain it there with overflow-x:hidden + max-width:100vw on a wrapper that is NOT an ancestor of .pillars-pin-wrap. Alternative: wrap .pillars-pin-wrap in its own scroll context using a parent without overflow rules. After fix, verify pin.getBoundingClientRect().top === 0 while scrollY is inside the 340vh wrap range.

LOW: useFitText could shrink the mobile footer wordmark one extra step so the element's scrollWidth (354px) equals its clientWidth (350px) at 390px viewport (currently 4px inner overflow, not visually clipped but technically not perfectly fitted).
INFO (carried from iter 1, optional): Remove 'frame-ancestors' directive from the CSP meta in index.html — browsers ignore frame-ancestors from <meta> and log noisy errors.
INFO: Cloudflare beacon script is blocked by the strict script-src CSP — injected by the Emergent preview proxy, not the app; no action needed.
critical_code_review_comments: BUG ROOT-CAUSE — styles.css:57 'html{overflow-x:hidden}' breaks position:sticky for ALL descendants. Sticky relies on a scrolling ancestor; setting overflow-x:hidden on html (paired with default overflow-y:visible) silently becomes overflow:auto/scroll in the cross-axis and changes the sticky containing block. This is the most likely reason the pillars pin animation that the user explicitly asked to be fixed still isn't visually pinning, even though the scroll-progress JS works correctly.

main.tsx is 1533 lines — should be split per code-review guidelines (>700 lines). Header, Hero, Pillars/Scrub, Stats/CountUp, Bento, Trainer, Roadmap, FAQ, Legal/Cookie modals, WaitlistForm should each be their own module.

WaitlistForm shares state between hero and footer instances by design; submitting on the hero shows the success message only in the hero copy, and vice versa — but BOTH forms re-render with each other's input value, which can confuse a user who submits at hero, scrolls down, sees their email pre-filled but no confirmation. Consider per-instance local state OR a single global toast.

Form has type='email' + required without noValidate, which means HTML5 popup intercepts the app-level error message 'Skriv en gyldig emailadresse.' for cases like 'abc' (no @). The app-level regex check is dead code for those inputs. Add noValidate to the <form> (or strip the email type) so the friendlier app-level Danish message actually surfaces to users typing malformed addresses.
Supabase anon key embedded client-side (acceptable for anon-only INSERT with RLS) — confirm prelaunch_waitlist_signups RLS allows only INSERT for anon, no SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE.

rca_of_the_issue: User complaint: 'Tre faser. Ét samlet flow.' animation isn't working / phone doesn't pin. Investigation: (1) The JS scroll-progress handler IS correctly computing pProg from window.scrollY relative to pillarsRef and updating pActive 0→1→2, the rail width 0→100%, and shot 'active' classes in sync — verified by reading classList and computed opacities at 6 different scroll positions inside the 340vh wrapper. (2) HOWEVER, the visual pinning fails: getBoundingClientRect().top of .pillars-pin equals .pillars-pin-wrap.top at every scroll position, meaning sticky is inactive. (3) Root cause: 'html{overflow-x:hidden}' at /app/src/styles.css line 57 — this is the canonical 'sticky breaker' (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/position#sticky_positioning — sticky requires the scroll-container ancestor to NOT have overflow:hidden/scroll/auto unless it itself is large enough to scroll). When html has overflow-x:hidden, browsers (Blink especially) treat html as the scroll container in a way that disables sticky calc for the body subtree. Fix: drop overflow-x:hidden from html (and ideally from body), and constrain the actual leaking element (a child of body) instead — typical culprits on this page are the .hero-canvas (full-bleed), the .trust marquee, and the giant .footer-word. After removing html overflow-x, the sticky should activate; the iteration_1 12px-on-mobile overflow concern that this rule was masking has ALREADY been fixed by other means (verified diff=0 in this iteration), so removal should be safe.
